message.content: The exact number of mitochondria varies widely between cell types and physiological conditions, but a typical mammalian cell contains on the order of **hundreds**—roughly **100–200 mitochondria**. Some highly active cells (e.g., muscle or liver cells) can have several thousand, while others may have only a few dozen.
